RESEARCH ONLY. Do not write files or code. Return findings as your final message text. Use curl via Bash for LIVE API probing (prefer live evidence) plus WebFetch/WebSearch for docs and terms. Cite a URL for every factual claim. QUOTE legal clauses verbatim.

Context: a game-server HOSTING company is building a mod/plugin catalog + one-click server-side installer. They ALREADY have Modrinth covered. Research every OTHER Minecraft plugin/mod source:

=== 1. SpigotMC (https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/) ===
- Is there an OFFICIAL API? (I believe not — verify and say so.) Any official statement from SpigotMC about scraping/APIs? Check https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/ and their ToS https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/spigot-rules/ or /help/terms.
- The UNOFFICIAL spiget API: https://spiget.org and https://api.spiget.org/v2/ . LIVE TEST these endpoints with curl and report actual fields:
  * GET https://api.spiget.org/v2/resources?size=3
  * GET https://api.spiget.org/v2/resources/{id}  (use a real popular plugin id, e.g. EssentialsX or Vault or LuckPerms — find one via /v2/search/resources/{query})
  * GET https://api.spiget.org/v2/resources/{id}/versions/latest
  * GET https://api.spiget.org/v2/resources/{id}/download  — does it actually return the jar? For "external" resources (external:true / file.externalUrl) what happens? This is important: many Spigot resources are hosted externally (GitHub, their own site) and premium resources cost money — report how the API flags premium (`premium: true`, `price`, `currency`) and external files.
  * GET https://api.spiget.org/v2/resources/{id}/author , /v2/authors/{id}
  * icon fields (icon.url / icon.data base64), tag, testedVersions, releaseDate/updateDate, downloads, rating, links.
- Does spiget expose a LICENSE field at all? (Verify — I suspect not.) How does Spigot handle licensing of resources?
- spiget rate limits (check response headers x-ratelimit-*), and its documented usage terms / who runs it (InventiveTalent). Is depending on it risky for a commercial product? Check its GitHub (github.com/InventivetalentDev/Spiget) and status.
- Also mention spigotmc's own `https://api.spigotmc.org/legacy/update.php?resource=<id>` (version-check-only, official-ish) and the SpigotMC "Restricted"/premium resource rules — QUOTE the SpigotMC rules about redistributing premium resources.

=== 2. PaperMC Hangar (https://hangar.papermc.io) ===
- Official API at https://hangar.papermc.io/api/v1/ — docs at https://hangar.papermc.io/api-docs or the OpenAPI spec. LIVE TEST:
  * GET https://hangar.papermc.io/api/v1/projects?limit=3
  * GET https://hangar.papermc.io/api/v1/projects/{author}/{slug}  (find a real one)
  * GET https://hangar.papermc.io/api/v1/projects/{slug}/versions
  * the download endpoint: /api/v1/projects/{slug}/versions/{name}/{platform}/download  — verify unauthenticated download works
  * auth: /api/v1/authenticate with an api key — is read access anonymous? What are the rate limits for anonymous vs authenticated?
- Report full field list for a project: namespace, name, description, category, lastUpdated, visibility, avatarUrl, stats (views/downloads/stars/watchers), settings (license {name, url, type}, links, tags, keywords, donation, forumSync), supportedPlatforms. Does Hangar expose LICENSE? (I believe YES — confirm with a live example and show the shape.)
- Hangar/PaperMC terms of service and privacy: https://papermc.io/terms or hangar's ToS. Quote anything about API use, caching, redistribution.
- Also note: is Paper/Velocity/Waterfall itself downloadable via an API? https://api.papermc.io/v2/projects/paper — document it (this matters for a hosting installer).

=== 3. Bukkit / dev.bukkit.org ===
- Confirm it is now part of CurseForge and what that means (gameId/classId for Bukkit plugins in the CurseForge API). Is the old ServerMods API (https://api.curseforge.com/servermods/files?projectIds=) still alive? Test it. Cite.

=== 4. Planet Minecraft (https://www.planetminecraft.com) ===
- Is there any public API? (Probably not.) Check for any documented endpoints/RSS/JSON. QUOTE their Terms of Use https://www.planetminecraft.com/terms/ or /account/terms/ especially anything about scraping, automated access, reproduction of content, and commercial use.
- What content types live there (worlds/maps, skins, texture packs, projects) and how download links work (are they direct? do they require the site?).

=== 5. Anything else notable for Minecraft server-side ===
- BuiltByBit (formerly MC-Market) — API? terms?
- Polymart (https://polymart.org) — it HAS an API (https://polymart.org/wiki/API or api.polymart.org). Test/describe briefly.
- Jenkins/CI-based plugin sources (e.g. ci.ender.zone, ci.lucko.me) and GitHub Releases for open-source plugins.
- Modpack sources relevant to servers: FTB app API (api.feed-the-beast.com / api.modpacks.ch), Technic Platform API (api.technicpack.net).

Be thorough and prefer live curl evidence. Be explicit about what you could not verify.

## Recipes

Wireless Redstone Trigger (receiver):

|   | Redstone |   |
|---|----------|---|
| Redstone | Target | Redstone |
|   | Redstone |   |

Wireless Redstone Remote (activator):

|   | Ender Pearl |   |
|---|-------------|---|
|   | Stick |   |
|   | Redstone |   |

## Usage

1. Place the Wireless Redstone Trigger block next to any block that receives redstone.
2. Right-click the Trigger block with the Remote
3. Every time you right-click the Remote, the Trigger block will provide a redstone signal.
   It will also update the trigger block which means it can trigger an observer block aswell.
4. You can also put a linked Remote in a **Dispenser** (not a Dropper) and power the dispenser
   with redstone - it will fire the signal instead of ejecting the stick.

The Remote's linked coordinates are shown in its tooltip (lore), useful for the player getting your items back after some PvP to find the activator's location!
To counter that, you can apply Curse of Vanishing to the remote to make it dissapear on your death.

### 1c. Downloads — this is where Spiget breaks for your use case

Three distinct behaviors, all live-tested:

**Free + Spigot-hosted → works.** `/v2/resources/28140/download`:
```
302 → https://cdn.spiget.org/file/spiget-resources/28140.jar
200  content-type: application/java-archive  content-length: 1501521
file: Zip archive data  ✅ real jar
```

**External → returns an HTML web page, not a jar.** EssentialsX (9089) is `"external": true` with `file.type: "external"`, `file.size: 0`:
```
302 → https://github.com/EssentialsX/Essentials/releases/tag/2.22.0
200  content-type: text/html
```
That is the GitHub **release tag page**, not the asset. The `/download/proxy` variant returned 291KB of GitHub HTML too. An installer following this blindly writes an HTML file into the plugins directory. **You must branch on `external` before every download** — Spiget's own spec says so: *"The `external` field of a resource should be checked before downloading, to not receive any unexpected data"* ([swagger.yml L188](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpiGetOrg/Documentation/master/swagger.yml)).

**Premium → 404.** Citizens (13811), `premium:true`, non-external:
```
302 → https://cdn.spiget.org/file/spiget-resources/13811.jar
404  {"code":"not_found","message":"File with such name does not exist.","status":404}
```
Spiget does not mirror paid jars. Good — but it means premium entries are catalog-only dead ends.

**Version pinning is effectively broken.** This is the finding I'd flag hardest. `/download` (no version) hits the CDN and works. But `/versions/{id}/download` redirects to spigotmc.org itself and dies on the Cloudflare challenge:

```
$ curl -L "https://api.spiget.org/v2/resources/28140/versions/590885/download"
302 → https://spigotmc.org/resources/28140/download?version=590885
301 → https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/28140/download?version=590885
403  cf-mitigated: challenge   ("Just a moment...")
```

Same 403 for `versions/latest/download`. **Spiget can only reliably serve the single latest jar per resource**, from `cdn.spiget.org/file/spiget-resources/<id>.jar`. For a hosting installer where "pin the version that matches the customer's MC version" is table stakes, that's disqualifying on its own.

### 1d. No license field — confirmed

Correct, you suspected right. `license` appears **nowhere** in the Spiget schema — I grepped the swagger and censused live responses; the only `license` hit in swagger.yml is Spiget's *own* Apache-2.0 license in the `info` block. SpigotMC has no license field in its resource model at all: authors state licensing in prose inside the (base64) description, or not at all. There is no machine-readable licensing on this entire source. For a commercial catalog that is a serious gap — you cannot programmatically answer "am I allowed to redistribute/install this."

### 1e. Rate limits and operator risk

No `x-ratelimit-*` headers on any Spiget response. 20 rapid sequential requests: all 200. Spiget's swagger documents only a prose warning on the proxy download: *"Note: this endpoint has a pretty strict rate-limit - cache downloaded versions locally and avoid repeated requests."*

Operator: **inventivetalent** (`info@inventivetalent.org`), org [SpiGetOrg](https://github.com/SpiGetOrg), Apache-2.0. Maintenance is alive but thin — `api.spiget.org` last pushed 2025-09-21, `SpigetFetcher` 2025-12-19, `spiget.org` 2026-07-03. Several repos archived. Single-maintainer, hobby-funded (site credits JetBrains and Aternos as supporters).

**The risk signal I'd weight most:** the org contains a repo named **`spiget-puppeteer-client`**. Spiget gets its data by driving a headless browser against spigotmc.org to defeat Cloudflare. It is an adversarial scraper of a site that is actively blocking scrapers. That's a structurally fragile dependency — it breaks whenever Cloudflare tightens, and it puts you downstream of conduct SpigotMC explicitly prohibits.

### 1f. SpigotMC's legal position — verbatim

`www.spigotmc.org` is fully bot-hostile: **even `/robots.txt` returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare JS challenge.** WebFetch and curl with full browser headers both 403'd. I retrieved the text from the Wayback Machine.

From [Spigot Forum Rules](https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/spigot-rules/) (snapshot 2026-09-03, page dated Jul 19 2025):

> **"Do not distribute "Premium Resources" to those who have not purchased them."**

> **"Do not access the forums via automated mechanisms."**

> "Using pay-per-click sites such as adf.ly or similar services to distribute resources is forbidden. External resource download URLs must be a direct link."

> ""Premium Resources" are held to a higher standard of originality and have greater punishments associated with breaching of these rules."

> "Posting someone else's plugin or resource is not allowed. This includes minor edits such as configuration changes and code taken directly from tutorials or other resources."

From the [SpigotMC Terms of Service](https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/spigot-terms/) (snapshot 2025-12-03), §4 "Use of the Platform":

> **"You may not copy, distribute or disclose any part of the Platform in any medium, including without limitation by any automated or non-automated "scraping";"**

> **"You may not use any robot, spider, crawler, scraper or other automated means or interface not provided by us to access the Platform or to extract data;"**

> "You may not share your license or access with any other parties;"

§12 Intellectual Property:

> "You agree to not engage in the use, copying, or distribution anything contained within the Platform unless we have given express written permission."

**Read plainly:** SpigotMC prohibits scraping and prohibits third-party interfaces "not provided by us." Spiget is exactly such an interface. `api.spigotmc.org/simple/0.2/` and `/legacy/update.php`, by contrast, *are* provided by them — which is the one defensible reading for using those two while avoiding Spiget.

### Auth and rate limits — quoted from the spec's own `info.description`

> "There are two ways to consume the API: Authenticated or anonymous. **When using anonymous authentication, you only have access to public information**, but you don't need to worry about creating and storing an API key or handing JWTs."

> "Send a `POST` request with your API key identifier to `/api/v1/authenticate?apiKey=yourKey`. The response will contain your JWT as well as an expiration time. Put this JWT into the `Authorization` header of every request and make sure to request a new JWT after the expiration time has passed."

> "**Please also set a meaningful `User-Agent` header.** This allows us to better identify loads and needs for potentially new endpoints."

> "### Rate Limits and Caching — **The default rate limit is set at 20 requests every 5 seconds with an initial overdraft for extra leniency.** Individual endpoints, such as version creation, may have stricter rate limiting. **If applicable, always cache responses.** The Hangar API itself is cached by CloudFlare and internally."

> "Note that all routes **not** listed here should be considered **internal**, and can change at a moment's notice. **Do not use them.**"

Confirmed live: `POST /api/v1/authenticate` with no key → `{"title":"Bad Request","status":400,"detail":"Required parameter 'apiKey' is not present."}`. 20 rapid GETs all returned 200. No `x-ratelimit-*` headers exposed — the documented 20/5s is your only signal, so self-throttle.

**Rate limits are identical for anonymous and authenticated** — auth buys you private content and write access, not throughput.

### Two endpoints worth designing around

- **`GET /api/v1/versions/hash/{sha256}`** — reverse-lookup a jar by hash. Verified live: feeding ViaVersion's sha256 returned the full project. This lets you identify plugins a customer uploaded manually, detect outdated installs, and spot tampered jars. No other source offers this.
- **`GET /api/v1/platforms/{platform}/versions`** — authoritative MC version list per platform, with `subVersions` grouping (`26.3`, `26.2`, `26.1`→`[26.1.2,26.1.1,26.1]`, `1.21`→`[1.21.11…1.21]`). Use this to build your compatibility matrix rather than parsing Spigot's freeform `testedVersions` strings.

Also available: `/latest`, `/latestrelease`, `/stats`, `/members`, `/stargazers`, `/watchers`, `/pages/main/{project}`.

### Hangar legal

[Hangar Terms](https://hangar.papermc.io/terms): **no clauses at all** about API use, automated access, scraping, caching, redistribution, or commercial use. Creators retain rights — *"You retain any and all of Your rights to any Content You submit, post, or display on or through the Service"* — and grant Hangar *"the right and license to use, modify, publicly perform, publicly display, reproduce, and distribute such Content on and through the Service."* Note that grant is scoped to *"on and through the Service"*, so your right to redistribute a given jar comes from **that project's own license**, not from Hangar. Which is exactly why the `settings.license` field matters.

[Hangar Guidelines](https://hangar.papermc.io/guidelines): *"You are not allowed to re-upload resources of other authors as-is."* And critically for you — **paid plugins are banned outright**: *"Functionality may not be hidden behind a paywall or an author-granted license key."* So **everything on Hangar is free by policy.** No premium-flag logic needed. No rules governing third parties who index or mirror.

PaperMC's other legal pages live at [forums.papermc.io/help/terms](https://forums.papermc.io/help/terms/), `/help/privacy-policy/`, `/help/legal-notice/`.

[Terms of Service](https://builtbybit.com/wiki/terms) §2 "ACCESSING OUR SERVICES", verbatim:

> **"Our Services includes a REST API through which we allow certain users certain levels of access to various information made available through our Services. Any sort of automated interfacing with our Services outside of our REST API is prohibited unless explicit permission is granted. Moreover, you agree not to crawl or scrape our Services for information, nor to utilize information made available through our Services in reproducing or reconstructing areas of our Services externally without explicit permission from us."**

That last clause — *"reproducing or reconstructing areas of our Services externally"* — is **a plugin catalog, described exactly.** Even using their sanctioned API, mirroring their marketplace into your catalog needs explicit written permission. Also relevant: sellers grant BBB *"a perpetual, unlimited, non-exclusive, royalty free license to host, copy, modify, distribute, sell and sublicense"* their content — that license runs to BBB, not to you.

It's a paid marketplace: downloads are purchaser-scoped. **Not catalogable without a partnership conversation.** They do maintain wiki pages on "Redistribution rights", "Server jar policies", "Anti-leak policies" and "Resource EULAs" that would be worth reading if you pursue this — I could not extract their bodies (JS-gated in Wayback snapshots; only navigation chrome rendered).

### GitHub Releases

The right primary source for the ~50 open-source plugins that matter most — and the real home of most Spigot `external:true` resources (EssentialsX, ViaVersion, SkinsRestorer, ViaBackwards all point there). Gives you the actual asset URLs Spiget fails to resolve, **plus a real license** via `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/license`.

**Rate limit is the constraint:** unauthenticated is 60 requests/hour — I exhausted it mid-research (`x-ratelimit-limit: 60, x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`). Use a token (5,000/hr) and cache aggressively; at 60/hr you cannot even refresh a 50-plugin catalog hourly.

## Recommendation

**Build the catalog on Hangar + GitHub Releases + PaperMC Fill v3, and add ServerMods as free long-tail coverage.** That set gives you machine-readable licenses (Hangar/GitHub), sha256 or md5 verification (Hangar/Fill/ServerMods), real dependency metadata (Hangar), anonymous access, documented rate limits, and no terms that prohibit what you're doing. Hangar is small (3,833 projects) but it's the curated, free-by-policy, legally clean core — and its hash-lookup endpoint gives you a genuine feature nobody else can.

**Treat SpigotMC as metadata-only, via the official `simple/0.2` API, and do not ship Spiget-backed installs.** Three independent reasons, any one sufficient: SpigotMC's ToS prohibits third-party scraping interfaces in terms that name exactly what Spiget is; there is no license field anywhere in the source, so you cannot establish a right to redistribute; and version-pinned downloads are simply broken (403 behind Cloudflare), leaving you able to serve only each plugin's latest jar. If you want Spigot-discovered plugins installable, resolve them to GitHub Releases by `sourceCodeLink` and install from there — that converts a legally and technically shaky path into a clean one.

**Exclude Planet Minecraft.** Five separate ToS clauses prohibit it, and they enforce.

The one item I'd action before anything else: **your installer's PaperMC integration is on a sunset API.** `api.papermc.io/v2` returns `{"ok":false,"error":"sunset"}` for paper, velocity, waterfall and folia. Migrate to `fill.papermc.io/v3` and add the mandatory identifying User-Agent — without it you're non-compliant with their stated policy, and the old endpoints are already returning errors rather than jars.
